titulo: A Short History of Spacecraft Landings on the Moon

fuente.licencia: Dominio público (VOA, gobierno de EE. UU.)
fuente.nota: Text shortened by removing paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: Many years have passed since the first spacecraft landed on the moon in 1966. From then until now, there have been many additional attempts with some succeeding and others failing. Here is a short history of some of these attempts.

The Soviet Union’s Luna 9 spacecraft was the first to land on the moon. It touched down on the lunar surface in 1966. The landing came after several other Soviet spacecraft either did not reach the moon or crashed on the surface.

The American space agency NASA says Luna 9 was the first spacecraft to carry out a soft landing on the moon. It was also the first to send “photographic data” from the moon’s surface to Earth. Luna 9’s landing proved “the lunar surface could support the weight of a lander and that an object would not sink into a loose layer of dust as some models predicted,” NASA said.

In May 1966, the United States followed with its Surveyor 1 mission. NASA describes this effort as “the first of a series of seven robotic spacecraft sent to the moon to gather data in preparation for NASA's Apollo missions.” The successful soft landing of Surveyor 1 “was one of the great successes of NASA's early lunar and interplanetary program.”
Both the U.S. and Soviet Union had other successful robotic landings. Next, the countries aimed to be the first to land humans on the moon.

In 1969, NASA successfully landed Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the moon. The U.S. Apollo program sent 12 astronauts to explore the moon over six missions. Apollo 17 was the last in 1972. The U.S. is still the only country to land humans on the moon. NASA officials say the agency’s Artemis program aims to return astronauts to the lunar surface possibly by the end of 2026.

In 2013, China became the third country to successfully land a spacecraft on the moon. China landed an exploring vehicle, or rover named Yutu that year. China followed with the Yutu-2 rover in 2019, this time touching down on the moon’s unexplored far side.

In 2020, China successfully returned samples of rock and dirt collected by the rovers. The mission returned about 1.7 kilograms of lunar material collected from the near side of the moon. Then in 2024, another mission returned rock and soil samples from the less explored far side of the moon. China has said it aims to land its astronauts on the moon by 2030.

In 2023, Russia tried its first moon landing in nearly 50 years. The Luna 25 spacecraft was attempting to land near the lunar south pole. But it is believed to have crash landed on the moon’s surface. The country’s last effort before that, Luna 24 in 1976, landed successfully and returned moon rocks to Earth.

After its first lander crashed into the moon in 2019, India made its second attempt in 2023. The country successfully landed its Chandrayaan-3 spacecraft on the lunar surface. The mission made India the fourth nation to complete a moon landing.

In January 2024, Japan became the fifth country to successfully land a spacecraft on the moon. But the SLIM spacecraft landed upside down. This caused some power and communication problems, but the lander was able to operate for a short time.
titulo_es: A short history of spacecraft landings on the Moon
resumen_es: A chronological review of Moon landings from the Soviet Luna 9 in 1966 to the recent missions of China, Russia, India and Japan, including the Apollo programme.
nivel_motivo: Although there are technical terms (lander, rover, soft landing), the structure is chronological, the sentences are short and the content is very predictable, which places it at B1.

ideas_clave.idea: Since the first lunar landing in 1966, there have been numerous attempts to reach the Moon, some successful and some not.
The Soviet probe Luna 9 achieved the first soft landing in 1966, sent the first images from the surface and showed that the ground could bear a spacecraft's weight.
The United States followed with Surveyor 1, part of a robotic series preparing the Apollo missions, before both powers raced to put people on the Moon.
With Apollo 11 in 1969 and five later missions, the US remains the only nation to have landed astronauts, and it plans to return through the Artemis programme.
China became the third country to land on the Moon in 2013, reached the far side in 2019, brought back samples from both sides and aims to send astronauts by 2030.
Russia's first attempt in almost five decades, Luna 25, apparently crashed in 2023.
India succeeded in 2023 after an earlier failure, and Japan became the fifth country in 2024, although its probe landed upside down.

resumen_modelo: The text offers a brief chronology of lunar landings since 1966. That year the Soviet probe Luna 9 achieved the first controlled landing, transmitted images to Earth and proved that the surface could support a spacecraft. A few months later, the United States landed Surveyor 1, the first of several robotic missions preparing the Apollo programme. In 1969 Apollo 11 put the first astronauts on the Moon, and the US remains the only country to have done so, although it intends to return under the Artemis programme. Decades later, new players emerged: China landed in 2013, reached the far side in 2019 and has since brought back samples. By contrast, Russia's Luna 25 crashed in 2023, while India and Japan landed successfully in 2023 and 2024 respectively.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Luna 9 was the first Soviet spacecraft ever sent to the Moon.
preguntas.cita: The landing came after several other Soviet spacecraft either did not reach the moon or crashed on the surface.
preguntas.explicacion: Luna 9 was the first to touch down, but before that the USSR had sent other spacecraft that did not get there or crashed.

preguntas.pregunta: What did Luna 9's landing prove, according to NASA?
opciones: That there was water on the Moon
That a lander would not sink into the lunar dust
That humans could breathe on the Moon
That the far side of the Moon could be explored
respuestas: That a lander would not sink into the lunar dust
preguntas.cita: an object would not sink into a loose layer of dust as some models predicted
preguntas.explicacion: It showed that the surface could support the weight of a lander and that the lander would not sink into the dust. Water and breathing are not mentioned, and China reached the far side much later.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 2 an expression that means “a controlled Moon landing, without crashing”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find an expression meaning 'a controlled landing without crashing'.
preguntas.cita: Luna 9 was the first spacecraft to carry out a soft landing on the moon
preguntas.explicacion: A “soft landing” is a gentle or controlled landing. In economics the same expression refers to a “soft landing” of the economy after a period of growth.

preguntas.pregunta: What was the purpose of the Surveyor series?
opciones: To bring lunar rocks back to Earth
To gather data in preparation for the Apollo missions
To land the first astronauts on the Moon
To explore the lunar south pole
respuestas: To gather data in preparation for the Apollo missions
preguntas.cita: sent to the moon to gather data in preparation for NASA's Apollo missions
preguntas.explicacion: The Surveyor craft were robotic probes sent to collect data before the Apollo programme. They did not bring back samples, they carried no astronauts, and the south pole is mentioned in connection with Luna 25.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: The Apollo program sent 12 astronauts to the Moon over six missions.
preguntas.cita: The U.S. Apollo program sent 12 astronauts to explore the moon over six missions.
preguntas.explicacion: The text says so explicitly: twelve astronauts on six missions, the last one in 1972.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: The Artemis program will include the first woman to walk on the Moon.
preguntas.explicacion: The text only says that Artemis aims to return astronauts to the Moon, perhaps in late 2026; it does not say who they will be.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 6 a word for an exploration vehicle that moves across the surface.
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word for an exploring vehicle that moves across the surface.
preguntas.cita: China landed an exploring vehicle, or rover named Yutu that year.
preguntas.explicacion: A “rover” is an exploring vehicle (es: astromóvil); the text itself defines it as an “exploring vehicle”.

opciones: It landed its first astronauts on the Moon
It returned samples from the far side of the Moon
It returned 1.7 kilograms of material from the near side
respuestas: It returned samples from the far side of the Moon
preguntas.cita: Then in 2024, another mission returned rock and soil samples from the less explored far side of the moon.
preguntas.explicacion: In 2024 it brought back samples from the far side. The 1.7 kg from the near side are from 2020, the first rover is from 2013 and astronauts are planned for 2030.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Russia's previous lunar mission before Luna 25 was a failure.
preguntas.cita: Luna 24 in 1976, landed successfully and returned moon rocks to Earth
preguntas.explicacion: The previous mission, Luna 24 in 1976, landed successfully and brought back Moon rocks; the one that failed was Luna 25 in 2023.

preguntas.pregunta: What happened to India's first lunar lander in 2019?
preguntas.cita: After its first lander crashed into the moon in 2019
preguntas.explicacion: The first Indian lander crashed. Landing upside down happened to the Japanese probe SLIM; the other options are not mentioned.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 10 an expression that means “the wrong way round, with the top at the bottom”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find an expression meaning 'with the top part at the bottom'.
preguntas.cita: But the SLIM spacecraft landed upside down.
preguntas.explicacion: “Upside down” means with the top at the bottom; do not confuse it with “inside out” (with the inside on the outside).

preguntas.pregunta: Why can Japan's moon landing be described as only a partial success?
respuestas: Because although SLIM did reach the surface, making Japan the fifth country to land on the Moon, it landed upside down, which caused power and communication problems and allowed it to work only briefly.
preguntas.cita: This caused some power and communication problems, but the lander was able to operate for a short time.
preguntas.explicacion: The answer must combine the achievement (fifth country to land on the Moon) with its limitations (upside-down position, power and communication problems, short operating life).

preguntas.pregunta: How has lunar exploration changed since the 1960s, according to the text as a whole?
respuestas: In the 1960s and 1970s it was a race between the US and the Soviet Union, culminating in the Apollo landings. Since 2013, new countries such as China, India and Japan have successfully landed on the Moon, while landings still often fail.
preguntas.cita: From then until now, there have been many additional attempts with some succeeding and others failing.
preguntas.explicacion: A global comprehension question: you need to contrast the space race between two superpowers with today’s wider range of countries, without forgetting that failures are still frequent.
